name: inkscape-text-on-path-bumper
story: A volunteer drew a full-frame competition bumper, curved the CHAMPIONS headline with Text > Put on Path, tucked the arc into <defs> so it stopped cluttering the layer list, and set the strap in DejaVu Sans - the font that was on their Linux machine.
idioms: <textPath xlink:href="#curve" startOffset="50%"> with the run wrapped in an inner <tspan>, the way Put on Path rewrites the text
the referenced <path id="curve"> sits in <defs> with style="fill:none;stroke:none" and sodipodi:nodetypes="cc"
stale x="420" y="560" left on the <text> from before it was put on the path
xmlns:xlink declared because Inkscape still writes xlink:href, not href, on textPath
-inkscape-font-specification:'Bebas Neue, Normal' - the family plus a style word, comma-separated
text-align:center;text-anchor:middle duplicated on the parent style and on the child
a <circle> written with cx/cy/r rather than Inkscape's sodipodi:type="arc" path, since it was drawn with the ellipse tool and then Ctrl+Shift+C'd
whyThisMatters: A curved headline is the one case where the promise says the field keeps its curve when the operator types, so this catches an importer that skips the run because its geometry reference lives in <defs>, that binds the inner tspan and loses the textPath on the first update, or that measures the field's box from the stale x/y and places the highlight 200px away from the words.
